text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila urges EU to take care that Europe does not lose its position as leading telecommunications continent, noting that much ground has been lost to the U.S. and Japan in consumer electronics.
- Government gave Finnish defense material firm permit to export armoured personnel carriers to Turkey. Cabinet divided on the issue.
- State betting company to introduce new "sabbatical" lottery ticket that will pay winner 10,000 markka per month for ten years.

- Ranking legal official, the parliamentary justice ombudsman, says Interior Ministry's instructions to mark foreigners' criminal records in their passports are illegal and against human rights norms.

- European Commision giving wholesale and retail group Kesko Oy a chance to alter its proposal on how to merge with Tuko to meet competition rules, but Kesko says cannot make new proposal before Commission's official ruling.
- Swedish insurer Skandia CEO said merger with major Finnish insurer Pohjola would be a "natural step," but that no merger talks under way.
- Copper prices could collapse if reports of secret copper stockpile in Holland are true and the metal comes onto the market, says metal and mining group Outokumpu.
- Sampo insurance chief Jouko Leskinen says banking group Merita should decide where it stands on its ownership stakes in Sampo and Pohjola insurance companies.
- Deutsche Bank Research believes Finland will be among first wave of countries in EMU, says currency union likely to expand rapidly by the year 2000 or 2001.
- Finns can't teach Chinese ping pong, but ice-hockey is another matter, said ice-hockey federation chief Kai Hietarinta. Finns to consult Chinese on hockey as part of cultural exchange.
- Former executives of Kansallis-Osake-Pankki (merged with Unitas into Merita) refuted all legal charges that they misled small investors in connection with a share issue in 1994 ahead of the merger.
- Finland has probably overtaken Sweden as country with highest per capita density of mobile phones, says Telecom Finland manager.
- Finnish science fiction writer Johanna Sinisalo's short story "The Red Planet" will be shipped to Mars aboard a space vessel to be launched from Kazakstan this weekend.
